mentions.name: Green Teeth
mentions.description: A DIY genetic engineering experiment in which the author modifies a probiotic strain (developed by Lumina, which may prevent cavities and colonize the mouth) to express sfGFP, so the author's teeth would glow fluorescent green under black light. It also serves as a direct way to observe microbiome changes shared between people who kiss.
mentions.problem: Microbiome research typically measures microbiome sharing indirectly via proxies; this experiment provides a direct, visible way to measure how microbiomes are shared while kissing.
mentions.audience: Personal experiment by the author, done for fun (e.g., glowing teeth at raves) and to explore microbiome sharing through kissing.
mentions.source_excerpt: Lumina has made a probiotic strain that is able to, theoretically, prevent cavities. I don't care that much about, but I do think it is a neat strain that can likely colonize your mouth. I'm genetically engineering it to express sfGFP, which would theoretically make my teeth fluorescent green under black light. Would be fun at raves!
